sentences.text: Agaleus was an extinct stem-galeomorph shark that lived during the Early Jurassic Epoch.
The species Agaleus dorsetensis is known only from isolated teeth.
While some authorities once placed Agaleus as a basal member of the order Orectolobiformes, later research classified it as a stem-galeomorph outside that crown group.
Fossils of Agaleus have been found in the Hettangian-Sinemurian of Lyme Regis, England, the Pliensbachian-aged Hasle Formation of Denmark, and the Grimmen clay pit in north-eastern Germany.
Remains have also been discovered in Northern Ireland, France, Belgium, and Sweden.
Agaleus lived from the Sinemurian to the Toarcian stages, between 199.5 and 174.7 million years ago.
